Thanks. I should explain a little, the Haario function is not the standard Haario, but is a lot more complex, as it has a banana for each pair of dimensions.
 
I also have some pictures showing the calculated v. analytic variance for these functions. Haario is excellent as a test because it is hard and the analytical solution is know.
 
The code for it (in Java) is:
 
            double a = 10.0;
            double b = 0.1;
            for (int iMod = 0; iMod < nMods - 1; iMod = iMod + 2) {
                grad[iMod] = -theta[iMod] / (a * a);
                logp += grad[iMod] * theta[iMod];
                double tmp2 = theta[iMod + 1] + b * (theta[iMod] * theta[iMod] - a * a);
                logp += -tmp2 * tmp2;
                grad[iMod + 1] = -tmp2;
                grad[iMod] += -2.0 * b * b * theta[iMod] * theta[iMod] * theta[iMod] - 2.0 * b * theta[iMod] * (theta[iMod + 1] - b * a * a);
            }
            logp = 0.5 * logp;
